title: The 5 Pillars of Data Transformation - Simply Explained
description:
Many organizations have Copilot, Power BI and Fabric, yet decisions still stall because nobody trusts the numbers or owns the call. This episode gives data and business leaders five pillars, from governance to human judgment, to test any report, prompt or flow before the next AI rollout.
In this episode
00:00 – Why faster AI answers still stall decisions00:50 – Pillar 1: Data governance04:14 – Pillar 2: Semantic layer07:20 – Pillar 3: Start with the decision10:18 – Pillar 4: Psychological safety13:42 – Pillar 5: Human judgment16:50 – Implementation and payoff
Key takeaways
AI moves bad data faster, so governance with named owners, sources and access rules has to come before automation.A semantic layer gives humans and AI one shared definition of business terms, and every report should start from a named decision and decision owner.Data transformation needs psychological safety to challenge the numbers and a named person who owns the final judgment on every AI-supported decision.
Worth quoting
“AI doesn't clean up confusion by itself. It can search across more files, summarize more records and send a recommendation in seconds. But it also moves bad data faster.” – Mirko Peters (01:00)
“Simply explained, it's a shared business dictionary with pre-approved calculations baked right in. You define a term once, store the logic once and reuse it everywhere” – Mirko Peters (04:39)
Explore more on M365.FM
Episode page: the full episode with chapters, quotes and a five-pillar FAQData governance – pillar one, setting owners, sources, access rules and quality checks before AI uses the dataSemantic model – a Power BI semantic model holds approved measures, relationships and field names in one layerHuman in the loop – why human review only counts when the person can still change the outcomeMicrosoft Purview – named as a tool for discovering data, applying sensitivity labels, tracking data movement and managing accessRelated episode: Microsoft Purview Unified Catalog - Simply Explained
